# IdeaBuilder framing (8020 compatible aluminum extrusion)

IdeaBuilder is 80/20 Inc.'s browser CAD for 8020 compatible aluminum extrusion T-slot frames. Opening and importing scenes works signed out; Save, Save to file, and every export (BOM CSV, Cut-List CSV, BOM XML, STEP, PDF) need a signed-in 80/20 Inc. account. An unsaved signed-out scene is lost if the browser closes, so keep a text build log (one line per step: part, face and end, Enter and Spacebar presses, length, entity count and price) to replay a rebuild.

## Pick the route first
- Each GUI step gets a 3-minute cap. If it fails, stop, note why, and switch route instead of retrying the same way.
- For a whole frame, the fastest reliable route is a hand-built scene JSON: generate it with a script from known-good template scenes (one exported example per part type), validate offline (FreeCAD copy, contact checks), then File > New and File > Import scene. A 108-entity frame and a 67-entity mixed test scene (members, brackets, feet, end caps, slot covers, pivot, linear bearing, door handle/latch/hinge, free accessory, Box Creator group) imported in one try.
- IdeaBuilder imports only its own scene JSON; it cannot read STEP or FreeCAD files. Its own exports re-import clean.
- Build a parts library as you go: for each new item type, place it once in a throwaway scene, Save to file, export BOM and cut list, and keep the JSON as that type's template.
- Round trip: after importing a generated file, Save to file and diff it against the source. The app renumbers ids, may add small fields (e.g. geom_dst on end-cap locators), and rounds floats, but it keeps locator positions exactly as written; it does not recompute them, so wrong locator data survives silently.
- If the native file dialog never appears for Import scene, set the file path on the page's file chooser directly from the browser tool. In a GTK dialog, type the path after Ctrl+L and click Select if Enter does not close it.
- When the app gets buggy, an export, close browser, import cycle can free it (exports need sign-in).
- Use the GUI for small edits to an imported scene (typed moves, lengths, single brackets).
- The bundled scripts (section below) cover the offline route end to end: generate, precheck, expected BOM and cut list, compare with the app's exports, FreeCAD copy.

## Lessons from GUI practice (summary, 2026-10-29)
- DEFINITION OF DONE: a frame is complete only after it is imported into IdeaBuilder and the app's own exports (Save to file JSON, BOM CSV, cut-list CSV) match the offline scene, BOM and cut list line by line (part number, qty, length per line). A matching price total is not a check. Until then, report it as not complete.
Many hours of GUI bracket practice on a lagged, software-rendered box produced at best 24 brackets in about an hour, while scene JSON imports went in clean on the first try. Rules that follow:
- Production route: lay out the frame in a script or FreeCAD, compute the joint fasteners in code (any fastener or combination shown strong enough, cheapest passing option wins; apply the free-cube rule so flush ends and other impossible joints are dropped before import), write the scene JSON, import, then verify in the app (all brackets grey, price matches the offline estimate, BOM and cut-list exports agree).
- GUI is for finishing: small edits, visual checks, and parts the generator can't write yet. It is not the way to place every bracket on a frame.
- Check the geometry before any GUI run: confirm member order, which ends are flush, and which joints can take a bracket. Never assume row order from the Entities list.
- Plan the path first (views, pans, orbits, rotation changes), then follow it. Pan and zoom until that view is used up, then orbit.
- Every GUI brief uses the same checklist: goal and stop point, time cap, allowed tools (including paced-drag helpers), known failure tips (re-arm a bracket that shows no ghost), the verified recipe, and what to screenshot. Don't rely on memory between runs.
- Hover points and press counts depend on the view; judge a bracket ghost by its shape, not by a remembered count.
- Solve each new GUI item once, save it as a template scene, and fold it into the generator so the skill turns into automation instead of repeated practice.
- Keep status messages to results, blockers and decisions.
- After any machine move, check that the browser and FreeCAD installs still exist before starting.

## Safety rules for any browser run
- Never open, hover, or click the Purchase menu (top bar, between Assembly and Support). The BOM is a File > Export item, not Purchase.
- No cart upload, quote, or order without the user's explicit OK.
- Click toolbar items by tooltip or label; hover to confirm the tooltip first.
- Never reload the tab; unsaved work is lost.
- With a member selected the XYZ gizmo is a move handle. Never left-drag it. Clear the selection before using any placement tool, unless the tool works on the selection (End Caps, Slot Covers). Start camera drags on empty canvas.
- Placement tools stay armed after a click; a stray click on EMPTY canvas drops a loose (often red) copy on the floor. Press Escape or pick the Select arrow after each placement and check the Entities list.
- Work on clearly named TEST copies; never overwrite a saved production design.
- Never show, type out, or screenshot a password. Paste from the clipboard into the masked field and clear the clipboard afterward.

## Browser setup
- Prefer FIREFOX on a box without a GPU. Chrome there renders WebGL with SwiftShader and lags 10 to 60 s per camera move, and its wheel zoom often dies. Firefox uses Mesa llvmpipe (still software) and answers zoom, pan, orbit and View-menu moves in about 2 s. If Firefox is missing and the distro package fails, the Mozilla tarball (download.mozilla.org, firefox-latest-ssl, linux64) unpacked to /opt works; launch it with its own --profile.
- Keep the browser window MAXIMIZED at 100% page zoom (Ctrl+0). A small window hides the top-toolbar camera icons (Pan, Orbit, Zoom, Undo).
- Software rendering repaints lazily: jiggle the mouse 1 px before a screenshot, wait 3 to 6 s after each action, and confirm results from the Entities list and price. Screenshots can run 1 to 3 actions behind; some screenshot readers cache by file name, so use a new file name every time.
- Scripted (in-page) mouse coordinates may not equal screen coordinates because of display scaling. Measure the mapping before any scripted press.
- Closing the browser window (not killing processes, which may hit other users of the same machine) and reopening gives a clean, empty scene, signed out.
- Keep parking clicks off panel headers: a click on the Entities header collapses the list.

## Keyboard (verified; the old Scribd shortcut PDF is partly out of date)
- T = change length: select an extrusion, press T, hover the small blue arrow on its end until it turns yellow, type the full mm value, press Enter. Hint bar: Ctrl = bigger snap distance, Shift = 45 deg angle connector.
- C = reset camera. F = fit to the SELECTED part (zooms very close), not the whole scene.
- Typed digits often drop (the leading digit or '-'). Check the box before Enter; if wrong, retype.
- Ctrl+A inside a dialog text field (e.g. the Save as name) can select all scene entities instead of the text. Triple-click the field to select its text.
- Typing into the Properties Length field can apply only the first digit; pick the autocomplete value, then Enter.
- Placement: ENTER = move the connection point to the next hole/cube, SPACEBAR = rotate around it. Keys only reach the app when the 3D view has focus: hover the canvas (click empty canvas first if a list had focus). After EACH press, wait about 4 s and take a fresh screenshot. Arrow keys, numpad and letter keys do not move the camera.

## Moving and copying
- Typed move: select the entity (Select arrow tool, then its Entities row), hover a red/green/blue move arrow until yellow, wait 2 s, type the distance, Enter.
- T swaps the gizmo to blue length arrows. A top-toolbar gizmo icon toggles the move arrows back.
- There is no copy command: Ctrl+C/V, the Edit menu and right-click have none, and synthetic Shift is ignored. To copy, typed-move the member to the new spot, then place a fresh one where it was.
- Moving a member drops the brackets and connections on it. That is real (it would happen in the shop too), not a bug: after a move, remove the stale brackets, rethink the joints at the new spot, and place them again.
- The Select arrow tool exits placement; Escape does not always.
- Toolbar Undo reverts the last placement reliably right after it, but avoid it for older steps (it can revert unrelated ones). Delete strays by selecting the Entities row, then the Delete key, the toolbar Delete icon, or Edit > Delete (the key does not always work). Deleting a bracket also deletes its screws and T-nuts.

## Camera
- The top toolbar has three camera MODE toggles: Pan, Orbit, Zoom. They are on/off toggles; a fresh session may start with Pan on or with all off, so clicking blindly can turn a mode OFF and drags then do nothing. Check the button highlight before clicking; click only to switch on an inactive mode.
- Desktop automation that sends a drag as one jump (press, one move, release) is ignored. Drive drags with a low-level input tool (e.g. xdotool on X11): mousedown 1, then about 10 relative moves of 10 px with about 50 ms between, then mouseup. Positioning works best as short scripted moves: move a little, look, adjust, move again.
- Firefox: the app ignores right and middle drags and modifier+left drags (Alt+drag moves the window instead). Orbit = Orbit mode + paced left-drag, about 50 deg yaw per 100 px horizontal (a full turn is about 700 px) and 30 to 35 deg pitch per 100 px vertical. TETHER: left-click a part to select it first, and the orbit pivots on that part (it stays fixed on screen while the view swings around it). With nothing selected the pivot is the world origin, and panning or Fit to selection do not move it, so high parts swing out of view. Observed 2026-10-28: a part selected from the Entities list (then View > Fit) did NOT act as the pivot, while a canvas left-click did; opening the View menu may clear the selection. Re-click the part on the canvas after Fit, before orbiting (unconfirmed).
- Pan = Pan mode + paced left-drag, about 1.3 px per px zoomed out and 2 px per px close in.
- Zoom: the wheel does nothing in Pan mode; in Zoom mode it zooms toward the screen centre in small steps, and a vertical drag in Zoom mode (up = in) is stronger.
- Fastest jump to a part: select its row in Entities, then View > Fit to selection (very tight; zoom out a little after). The View menu also has Fit all, Restore camera, Front/Back/Left/Right/Top/Bottom and Perspective/Orthogonal; hover an item about 1.5 s, then click.
- Chrome: a paced right-button drag that STARTS ON a member orbits around it (pivot = start point), with Orbit and Pan modes off.
- Opening the View menu clears the selection.
- View > Settings > Controls has only invert X, invert Y and invert zoom. View > Settings > DRAWINGS has angle, length and grid snaps plus strict series check and collision detection.

## Sign in
1. Click LOG IN. An in-page dialog opens; choose the 80/20 Inc. log-in option (the button reads LOG IN WITH followed by the company name), then fill email and paste the password.
2. The open scene survives sign-in without a reload.

## Files
- File menu: New, Open, Save as, Import scene, Documentation (PDF), Export scene as STEP, Export BOM as XML, Export BOM as CSV, Export Cut-List as CSV, Scene properties. Signed out, Save and the exports only say "You need to be logged in".
- File > New asks "clear current scene?" with OK only (no save option).
- Import scene MERGES into the open scene. Do File > New first.
- After Import scene every imported entity stays SELECTED. Pressing Delete then wipes the whole scene; the toolbar Undo restores it, Ctrl+Z does not. Click empty canvas to clear the selection before any key press.
- Save as opens on the Save to file tab with a STALE prefilled name; replace it and verify before saving. Saving renames the open scene.
- Exports download straight to the browser's download folder, prefixed with the scene name, no dialog.
  - BOM CSV: semicolon-separated; part number, description, quantity. Extrusion lengths there are labeled mm but are really INCHES; use the cut list for true mm. The BOM leaves out fasteners priced inside their part: when every appdata/ib_bolt_kits.json entry of the root part that names the fastener has assembly_uid null (2107 deadbolt: 3062 + 3382). Kits with an assembly_uid (4351 plates, 2085 hinge, 2060 handle, brackets) list their fasteners as their own BOM lines. scripts/make_expected.py applies this rule (verified by signed-in export, 2026-10-31).
  - Cut-List CSV: index; part number; length (mm); description; quantity, one row per cut length.
- Scene info Entities counts fewer than the file: sub-parts priced inside a kit (pivot plates, end-cap and latch fasteners) are not counted.
- Scene JSON is format 7, UTF-8 with BOM (read as utf-8-sig), column-major matrices, Y up. A joint is a connector_locators entry with an optional "connector" entity id. An injected bracket needs a screw child, a T-nut grandchild, connection_map entries and a connector_locator. T-nuts are children of their screw. Thin red marks at a member end mean the app thinks that end is not attached, even when it is; ignore them where the joint is real.

## Members
- First member: arm the profile (the T-slotted panel tile or Recents), click a start point on the ground grid, move, click to set the direction; then set the length with T. For a vertical member, press Spacebar after the start click, move the cursor up, then click.
- From a rail's end face the ghost only extends in line; build legs from the floor up.
- Attaching a member to another member commits only on a DOUBLE-click. It lands at about 30 mm; set the length after.
- Select a member's row in the Entities list to see Article, Length, Price, Weight, Finish, BOM Exclude, Machining.
- Red member = unconnected. A thin red or pink band at a member end is the app's unattached-end flag, shown even when the end is attached; ignore it if the joint is real.

## Placement tools (left toolbar, by tooltip)
Infill Panel, Mounted Panel, Feet and Casters, End Caps, Slot Covers, Tri-Corners, Pivots, Joint Plates, Corner Brackets & Gussets, Guarding System (next to Joint Plates; easy to arm by mistake), Door Parts, Door Creator, Contour Creator, Linear Bearings, Hardware & Accessories, Box Creator, Pipe, Flexpipe Accessory, Measure.

### Corner Brackets & Gussets (works with care)
1. Set a view where the inside corner and BOTH inner faces (one on each member) are visible, zoomed in close. Then click empty canvas once far from the frame so the 3D view has keyboard focus and nothing is selected.
2. Open the tool, pick the series and bracket (Recents is quicker once used; it is empty in a fresh session). If no ghost appears, click a different bracket and then the wanted one again.
3. Hover the member face right beside the corner, not the corner edge. Wait 4 to 6 s; the ghost lags and may show a stale spot.
4. The CONNECTION POINT shows on the ghost as a red/pink dot on one hole (easiest to see on multi-cube gussets). ENTER moves it to the next hole/cube; it must sit on the cube side touching the member near the corner. Press once, wait, screenshot.
5. SPACEBAR then rotates the bracket around that connection point. Press once at a time, wait about 4 s, screenshot, until one leg lies flat on each member inside the corner.
6. Single-click to place (commits on ONE click). Check the price rose by one bracket (bracket plus its auto fasteners) and look from a second angle; undo a bracket that lands on the outside of a rail or floating.
7. Grey = good. Red = its slots don't all land on free T-slot space (every hole cube must sit on whole, free member cubes; one cube = 38.1 mm on 15-series, 25.4 mm on 10-series). An existing bracket in the same slot can block it. FREE-CUBE RULE: a bracket needs a free cube on BOTH members. Where a member ends flush with the other (e.g. a ladder's top rung level with the upright ends), there is no cube on that end, so no pose, Space or Enter setting will ever place it grey. Check for the cube before trying; if the "Tetris" can't be completed, skip the joint (and plan another part, e.g. an end fastener).
8. SNAP: with the bracket already Space-rotated to the right pose and a clear line of sight to the inside corner (no upright, rung or bracket in the way), sweep the cursor toward the corner; the offset readout counts down and then jumps to the snapped spot (19.05 mm for a 4332 on 15-series). Click there. A snap does not override the free-cube rule.

### 4332 ladder recipe (15-series, verified 2026-10-28, Firefox)
- Before arming, click empty ground (clears selection, gives focus); arm the 4332 from Recents.
- Hover the rung face near the upright until the readout shows 19.05 mm (30 mm = one cube too far).
- Top faces: left joints Space x2, right joints Space x0.
- Undersides: select the rung (canvas click; see tether note), Orbit mode, paced left-drag down about 40 px x6, Fit to selection, hover near the upright end, left Space x2, right Space x0.
- Good bracket = +5 entities and +$9.87; red = +3 entities and +$8.80, undo it at once.
- Close the bracket palette (its icon top right) and press Escape before clicking Entities rows, or the click lands on the palette.
- TWO FLUSH ENDS (FreeCAD check, 2026-10-28): a ladder whose end rungs sit level with the upright ends has no top-face corner on the top rung and no underside corner on the bottom rung. Placeable = top faces of every rung except the top one + undersides of every rung except the bottom one (24 on a 7-rung ladder). In that ladder's Entities list, row 1 = bottom rung (y 0), row 7 = top rung; select row 1 first to confirm.
- Space rotation does NOT reset predictably between placements: judge the ghost by shape, not press count. Right-end good ghost: slotted-hole plate on the left, gusset triangle on the right; an octagon-hole plate facing you is wrong, press Space until the slot shows.
- Plan before running: convert the scene to FreeCAD (scripts/ib2freecad.py), work out which corners each camera direction sees, and plan a path with the fewest orientations (ladder: one view from above for all tops, left set climbing then right set descending; one orbit down for all undersides, right set climbing (Space carries over) then left descending), pan-only between corners, no per-rung Fit to selection.
- Result: 24 of 24 placeable brackets on a 72x12 in, 7-rung ladder (flush top rung excluded) in 1 h 03 min on the first full run: 129 entities, $466.74.

### Feet, casters, base plates (works)
1. Open Feet and Casters; tabs: Base Plates, Casters, Floor Mounts, Feet.
2. Pick the part, zoom so a post's bottom END is visible, hover the end, wait about 7 s for the ghost, click.
3. Stem feet and stem casters save as a top-level entity linked POINT_TO_POINT from the part's stem marker to the post's core-hole marker.
4. Flange-mount casters can preview snapped to a side slot yet land loose on the floor; check, and delete if loose.

### Linear bearings (works)
- Open Linear Bearings, pick the bearing for the series, hover the rail face until a ghost shows, click. The bearing snaps to the slot and adds its own screw and T-nut (saved as a point-to-line link to the slot).

### End Caps and Slot Covers (works: select first)
- End cap: select the post, then click End Caps. A cap goes on the top end at once, as a child of the post with its fastener.
- Slot covers: select the member, then click Slot Covers. One cover goes in every slot (4 on a 15-series square profile), as children of the member; cover length is the matrix scale. The BOM may show qty 1 for all of them.

### Pivots (works)
- Insert the pivot at a member end; the arm is a separate top-level member and its length is set in Properties. Set the angle in the Pivot angle field; the stored pivot_angle equals 90 minus the angle shown in the UI. The pivot plates are children and carry the rotation; the arm follows the angle.

### Door Parts (works in the GUI and offline)
- Handles, hinges and latches snap to a rail face and auto-add screws and T-nuts. Only the frame side of a hinge was tested.
- Offline route VERIFIED by import and by signed-in export compare (2026-10-31: BOM 8/8, cut list 2/2, scene 24/24, locators 20/20, ALL PASS once make_expected.py drops the kit-priced 2107 fasteners): scripts/ib_entities.py Scene.door_part(pn, rail, dist, slot) via scripts/gen_frame.py door. 2085 hinge (2 x 3340 + 2 x 3278), 2060 handle (2 x 3112 + 2 x 3278) and 2107 deadbolt with side latch (2 x 3062 + 2 x 3382) all imported grey on a 1515 frame. The 2107's 3062 + 3382 stay in the scene JSON but are NOT BOM lines (priced inside the 2107).
- Slot faces observed with slot 1 on a 1515 rectangle in the XY plane (front = +Z): hinge on the right stile and handle on the left stile both showed on the FRONT (outside) face, not facing into the opening; the deadbolt on the top rail showed on the underside, inside the opening. The script's locator data put the hinge holes on the stile's inner face, so the slot-to-face mapping for vertical stiles is not yet trusted: check from two angles and change --slot if a part lands on the wrong face.
- dist positions the part's root origin, which for 2107 is the centre of its two mounting screws. The deadbolt body is not symmetric about its screws and shows offset toward one end of the rail (toward the hinge side in the test); allow for it when centring.
- Scene info showed 20 entities for the 24-entity file (kit sub-parts are not counted, see Files), and its price read lower than the selection total.

### Hardware & Accessories
- Categories: Accessories, Electrical, Manifold Plate, Blocks, Other. Items place free-floating with no connection to members. No T-nuts or handles live here.

### Joint Plates (offline route works; native tool unsolved)
- Offline route VERIFIED by import and by signed-in export compare (2026-10-31: BOM 5/5, cut list 2/2, scene 48/48, locators 32/32, ALL PASS): scripts/ib_entities.py Scene.plate() writes 4351 / 4365 style plates with screws, T-nuts, links and locators from a bolt list (scripts/gen_frame.py plate). Four 4351 plates on the front face of a 1515 rectangle imported grey with their screws; Inspector name "15 S 5 HOLE 90 DEGREE JOININGPLATE". Deleting one plate removes 11 entities (plate + 5 x 3330 + 5 x 3278, priced as one kit). Use this route for plates.
- Native tool: plates show a grey ghost at a joint but come out red, even on a bare joint, with the toast "Not all accessory slots are attached to profile T-slots", no fasteners, and possibly placed away from the joint. Undo or delete it.

### Tri-Corners
- The tool may be broken; add tri-corners through Edit > Add extra parts (BOM only).

### Box Creator (works), Door Creator and native panel tools (unsolved)
- Box Creator takes three clicks and makes a group entity (template, w, l, h) of members with end fasteners, but no panels. Metric default sizes give non-whole-inch cuts; set inch sizes for real builds.
- Door Creator created nothing on hover or click.
- Infill Panel opens its catalog but shows no ghost and creates no panel. Mounted Panel enters a multi-click rectangle-drawing mode (not yet completed); an earlier try said "too small".
- Panels offline route VERIFIED by import (2026-10-31); export NOT yet verified: both an infill panel (in the frame opening, edges in the slots) and a mounted panel (on the front face) imported as normal, not red. Neither has links to the frame. The Inspector has NO Infill / Mounted field: it shows Article, Width, Height, Price, Weight, BOM Exclude, Machining; the type is implied by size and position only. Panel price is area-based (the 2651 1/4 in black HDPE test panels: 247.65 mm square and 304.8 mm square priced separately by area). In the BOM, expect each panel size priced by area; confirm the row form with a signed-in export.
- Panel export blocked by collision (two tries on 2026-10-31, later corrected). Both signed-in exports were refused by IdeaBuilder's pre-export collision check, so no BOM or cut list. At the second try the check flagged the INFILL frame, 1001-1004 (1515) plus 1005 (2651 infill, 247.65 mm square at z 0). The MOUNTED frame 2001-2005 (2651 at z 22.325) was clean. The earlier note said the mounted panel collided; that was WRONG. INFERRED: the first try's flagged set (2 x 228.6, 2 x 304.8, one 2651) was the infill frame too, since the same infill panel sat at z 0 there.
  Observed behavior (export tests and collision checks, 2026-10-31):
  (1) An infill panel whose origin sits on the slot mid-plane collides with all four members; with the origin moved back by half the panel thickness (2651: z -3.0) it exports clean. The panel body behaves as one-sided, extending from the origin along its normal by the panel thickness.
  (2) A profile behaves as its outer square with a notch per open T-slot; 1515 measures 8.13 mm wide x 12.3 mm deep, matching 80/20 Inc.'s 1515 drawing (0.320 in opening, 0.484 in face to cavity floor).
  (3) Linking a panel to its frame does not excuse panel-to-profile contact in the collision check.
  (4) The app's own Infill tool places the panel centred on the slot mid-plane.
  The old gen_frame put the infill origin ON the mid-plane, so the body spanned z 0 .. 6.0, and its front face cut 1.935 mm past the notch half-width (4.065) into all four members. The mounted body (22.325 .. 28.325) has a 3.275 mm gap to the face at 19.05, so it cannot collide. The 9.525 mm edge depth is fine: it is under the 12.3 mm notch depth, and 80/20 Inc.'s Panels & Doors catalog adds 0.750 in per dimension for a 15 Series panel resting in the slot.
  Fix (export-tested in the next item): gen_frame infill writes origin z = -t/2 with a counter-clockwise contour (or --flip: clockwise, origin +t/2, the app tool's own form). t comes from templates/appdata/panel_thickness.json. precheck_collision now models the one-sided body and the 8.13 x 12.3 slot notch, and reproduces the second try's result: 4 hits on 1001-1004 x 1005, 0 on the mounted frame. Do not turn off View > Settings > Drawings > collision detection to force an export unless the user agrees: it hides real overlaps.
- Panel export VERIFIED by signed-in export compare (2026-10-31): a centred infill test (origin z -t_app/2) and a mounted-only test both exported with no collision block and compare_exports ALL PASS (BOM 3/3, cut list 2/2, scene 5/5, locators 12/12); a flipped infill test (clockwise outline, origin z +3.0) also passed Edit > Collision check. In the BOM CSV the panel row reads '<PN>;<description> (<area> mm)' where the bracketed number is the panel AREA in square feet (INFERRED from two sizes) (247.65 mm square = 0.66, 304.8 mm square = 1), not mm; qty is the panel count.
- Panel entity form: a panel entity has template = panel PN, data.contours.PLN_CONTOUR (CURVE_POLYLINE, local XY, centred), normal = contour winding (counter-clockwise = local +Z; the body extrudes that way by the template thickness), optional MC_PANEL_NOTCH machining and PANELHOLE slots; no links to the frame. Infill size = clear opening + slot expansion per edge (15 Series 9.525 mm, 20 Series 5 mm, 25 Series 7 mm, from the app's code); app resource examples of mounted panels carry connection_user_prefs.panel_screw_steps (203.2 mm). scripts/gen_frame.py panel writes both forms for an import test. Hints: Infill Ctrl+click = gasket, Shift+click = retainers; Mounted Shift+click = mounting blocks. Door Creator hints: Ctrl = double door, Shift = bi-fold, wheel = door type.

### Edit > Add extra parts (BOM-only parts)
1. Edit > Add extra parts. Search by part number, click the row, set Add amount, press ADD >, then SAVE.
2. Price and Extra parts count update; entity count does not. A length-sold part (e.g. slot cover) takes its amount in mm.
3. Undo does NOT remove extra parts, and the red X in the dialog may not stick; check the BOM after.

## Speed
- Targets for a skilled user: about 30 s per two-member joint and 30 s per bracket. On a software-rendered box, budget the settle waits and keep steps small.
- Visiting every joint of a frame: select each member's Entities row, Fit to selection, then short pans to each end (a 14-joint ladder took 39 s this way in Firefox, against 224 s by manual pan and zoom in Chrome).

## Verify before handing off
1. Clear selection; record entity count and price.
2. Export BOM CSV, Cut-List CSV, BOM XML (signed in) and diff against the plan. Scene-info price may not equal the sum of BOM lines; note it rather than assume.
3. Confirm no unexpected red members or accessories.
4. Log what failed and what you tried, then move on rather than stalling.

## Bundled scripts (scripts/, data in templates/)
Plain python3 unless noted; every script prints its usage with --help. Details: scripts/README.md.
- scripts/gen_frame.py: small test frames (20 Series cube with 20-4119 corners, 15 Series plate / panel / door variants) with a report of free holes, seat gaps and off-grid cut lengths.
- scripts/ib_entities.py (15 Series), scripts/ib20.py (20 Series), scripts/ib25.py (25 Series), scripts/ib_core.py, scripts/jsnum.py: scene writers. jsnum writes JS-format numbers with the UTF-8 BOM the app expects.
- scripts/make_expected.py: expected BOM and cut list in the app's export format from a scene JSON.
- scripts/compare_exports.py: line-by-line multiset check of the app's BOM, cut list and saved JSON against the expected files (row order is INFO only; descriptions and price are not checks).
- scripts/precheck_collision.py: fast box-body collision precheck before import (bracket and plate bodies ASSUMED; panel body and 15 / 10 / 20 / 25 Series slot notches from the app code).
- scripts/ib2freecad.py, scripts/check_ib2freecad.py, scripts/intersect_scene.py (freecadcmd): FreeCAD copy, member and joint checks, solid intersections.
- scripts/build_library.py: add new item types to templates/examples from your own GUI saves.
- The reports flag members whose cut length is off a 1/8 in grid (useful when cutting on a chop saw).

## Data files you build yourself
This published copy ships the scripts and an empty scene header only. It does not ship the part library (templates/examples), the app data (templates/appdata), or the FreeCAD profiles (templates/profiles). Build them from your own sources:
- templates/examples: run scripts/build_library.py on your own IdeaBuilder GUI saves (see scripts/README.md).
- templates/appdata: the scripts read slot maps, bolt kits, price units and panel thicknesses from here. Fill it from your own signed-in IdeaBuilder session and exports; the scripts report which file is missing.
- templates/profiles: draw 2D profile sketches in FreeCAD from the free vendor STEP models, or set IB2FC_PROFILES to your own folder.

The FreeCAD conversion scripts and the 20 and 25 Series helpers are covered by the companion skill 'IdeaBuilder to FreeCAD tools (8020 compatible aluminum extrusion)'; both use the same repo and work folder.

# Getting started (Frame Builder)

You lay out 8020 compatible aluminum extrusion T-slot frames, produce the cut list, joints and cited BOM, build the frame in IdeaBuilder from generated scene JSON, and prove it with a line-by-line export check. Use the ideabuilder-framing-8020-compatible-aluminum-ext skill for all IdeaBuilder work.

Ask the owner these questions one at a time, waiting for each answer. Offer the default with each one so the owner can just say yes. Never ask two questions in one message.

1. Do you have a Frame Project Manager (8020 compatible aluminum extrusion) bot and a Custom Parts Designer (8020 compatible aluminum extrusion) bot? (Default: I look for them now; see below for running without them.)
2. Units for the world and the cut list: inches, millimeters, or mixed? (Default: inch cut lengths; profile sizes as 80/20 Inc. publishes them.)
3. What 8020 compatible aluminum extrusion stock do you own now: series and size measured across the face, stick count and lengths, any hardware? Or where should I check? (Default: none owned; every part is a buy line. With a project manager bot, it asks this per project.)
4. Starting defaults, confirmed again at each project's intake: saw kerf 1/8 in with no end trim; whole-inch cut lengths where practical and never finer than 1/8 in (metric: 5 mm, never finer than 1 mm); static safety factor 2; deflection target 1.5 mm at the stated load. Keep these as the starting set? (Default: keep all.)
5. Joint rule: any fastener or combination may be used, the cheapest one that passes the strength check wins, and every fastener is listed in the CAD model and the BOM? (Default: yes.)
6. Vendor order. (Default: the 80/20 Inc. store first, then McMaster-Carr, then marketplace sellers last and only when neither stocks the part. You can change it now or per project.)
7. IdeaBuilder access: will you sign in yourself when an export is needed, or save a login in the vault? (Default: you sign in; I work signed out until then. Exports need a signed-in account.)
8. Who buys? (Default: you buy. I never upload a cart, purchase, or request a quote.)
9. Ship-to: labels only (for example SHIP_TO_1), or "ask per project"? (Default: ask per project, confirmed before any order talk.)
10. Where should project folders live, and may the other bots read them? (Default: one folder per project; each bot writes only its own folder and reads the others'.)

After question 1 (finding the other bots):
- Look through the owner's bot roster for a project manager (intake, stock checks, reviews, decisions log) and a CAD bot (FreeCAD, interference or deflection checks, custom parts). Confirm each with the owner before saving its name and id as a memory.
- No project manager: I do intake, stock and KISS checks myself and report to you directly.
- No CAD bot: I run the collision precheck and the FreeCAD conversion and intersection scripts from the IdeaBuilder to FreeCAD tools skill myself, and say in each report that no deflection check was run.
- Offer each found bot a one-line intro, sent only with your OK for that message.

Finish setup:
- Save the answers as memories.
- Create the project folder root and an empty parts library folder for IdeaBuilder templates.
- Get the scripts: follow 'Bundled files: get them from the repo on first run' in the ideabuilder-framing-8020-compatible-aluminum-ext skill and in 'IdeaBuilder to FreeCAD tools (8020 compatible aluminum extrusion)': clone or download the repo into one work folder at the pinned full commit SHA those skills give (never a branch), and check every file against the SHA-256 list in those skills. If any file fails or is missing, stop, run nothing, and tell the owner.
- Run the self-test both skills describe (py_compile on every script, --help on each) and report pass or fail. Scripts that need templates/appdata stop until that data is built; tell the owner how to build it ('Data files you build yourself') instead of counting it as a failure.
- Ask for the first frame brief, or wait for the project manager's intake.md and stock.md.

Rules: Save to file only (no cloud saves unless the owner asks). Never change account settings. Never invent prices, part numbers or dimensions; cite the vendor page. Label anything undecided PROPOSAL. Plain text, no emoji, 24-hour times.

---
# Get a CAD model from McMaster-Carr

Rules: check local files first and never re-download something already fetched (search the CAD library folders on this computer and the user's machines for the part number). Browse at a normal human pace, one model at a time, only what the design needs; no scraping or bulk downloads.

1. In the signed-in browser, open https://www.mcmaster.com/ and search for the part type (e.g. `8020 compatible t-slotted framing`).
2. Narrow it with the left filter panel (profile, inch/metric, height, width, style) until the product table shows the right family.
3. In the table, click the part number for the exact size/finish wanted (e.g. `5537T912`). A detail popup opens.
4. In the popup's CAD row, choose `3-D STEP` from the dropdown and click `Download`. If a length or option is asked, pick the shortest (the model's length is changed in CAD).
5. The file lands in the browser's Downloads folder as `<PN>_<name>.STEP`. Move it into the project's CAD library folder and record the part number, description and product URL in that folder's README index.
6. If a sign-in, bot check or captcha appears, stop and hand the screen to the user. Never add to cart or order.
